info.bio: They Might Be Giants (comúnmente abreviado como TMBG) es una banda estadounidense de rock alternativo/universitario formada por John Linnell y John Flansburgh. Conocido por su experimental pop, el grupo ha sido popular en los campus universitarios estadounidenses y se ganó una reputación como banda de rock intelectual/empollón gracias a la poco convencional temática de su música, la cual a menudo contiene referencias a la historia, la ciencia, el cine, la literatura y la música de otros artistas.

scenes.name: College-pop y nacimiento del lo-fi
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La población universitaria del Sur adopta la ética de la new wave y la adapta a la melodía: un pop inusualmente intelectual, con raíces en el folk-rock y el country-rock pero contaminado por las neurosis de la época. Athens (Georgia) compite con las capitales del rock: B-52's y R.E.M., uno de los grupos de más éxito de la historia. Carolina del Norte (dB's, Windbreakers), Hoboken (Smithereens, Bongos, Tiny Lights), el nacimiento del lo-fi (Half Japanese, Violent Femmes, Beat Happening, Guided By Voices, Sebadoh), They Might Be Giants, Green, B.A.L.L., Boston (Volcano Suns, 10,000 Maniacs, Throwing Muses, Blake Babies), la Costa Oeste (Game Theory, Posies, Young Fresh Fellows) y la sátira de Ween.

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …in two camps: the street punks and the college kids. The genre peaked in the second half of the decade with consummate popsters such as New York's They Might Be Giants (3), i.e. John Flansburgh and John Linnel, who retained the satirical, offbeat quality of the punk era. Actually, the wit of They Might Be Giants (1986) recalled the British operetta, the music-hall, the Bonzo Band, Frank Zappa, Todd Rundgren, and the bubblegum novelties of the Sixties. In…

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …personal musica-hall, a gallery of comic/erotic vignettes that clung to musical nonsense and variety. The duo mastered the silly melodies of the They Might Be Giants and the bizarre arrangements of Mark Kramer, and proceeded to create a wildly eclectic opus. podcast.title: Formation and Early Innovation (1982)
podcast.body: The two-man group, consisting of John Flansburgh and John Linnell, formed in Brooklyn in 1982. They were known for their unusual projects, such as writing songs for their answering machine. "They've been around since 1982 doing weird things like writing songs for their answering machine."

podcast.title: Dial-a-Song Service (1986 On-Again, Off-Again)
podcast.body: Starting in 1986, They Might Be Giants maintained an on-again, off-again service called `Dial-a-Song`. This allowed people to call a specific number, and an answering machine would play a new original song. "and maintained an on-again, off-again service called Dial a Song, which is just like it sounds. They gave out a number, which you could call, an answering machine picked up, and then you would hear a new original song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Dial-A-Song" Service (716-387-6962)
podcast.body: The band established a unique service called "Dial-A-Song," which allowed fans to call a specific phone number (716-387-6962) to hear a new song daily or weekly. Although the number has been disconnected, it occasionally resurfaces, highlighting their pioneering use of interactive fan engagement. "They ran something called dial a song where fans could dial a number and get a new song every day, every week, whenever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Nerd Rock Kings" Designation
podcast.body: Billboard magazine eventually referred to They Might Be Giants as the "Nerd Rock Kings," a designation that may have been instrumental in bringing the term "nerd rock" into mainstream usage. "Billboard would eventually refer to them as the Nerd Rock Kings."

podcast.title: Children's Music Success (2000s)
podcast.body: By the 2000s, the group had a significant presence in children's music, releasing albums with educational titles such as `Here Come the ABCs`, `Here Come the 123s`, and `Here Come Science`. "By the 2000s, the group was actually releasing albums with titles like Here Come the ABCs, Here Come the 123s, and Here Come Science."

podcast.title: Diverse Creative Output
podcast.body: Beyond albums, They Might Be Giants have contributed to soundtracks and collaborated with magazines and journals, demonstrating a broad range of creative endeavors. "They've also written for soundtracks, work with magazines and journals."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Lo-fi Setup
podcast.body: In their early years, John Flansburgh handled vocals and guitar, while John Linnell provided backup on accordion and saxophone. They sometimes utilized a drum machine or played along to backing tracks pre-recorded onto a cassette. "The early years, John would sing and play guitar, while the other John would provide backup on a accordion and saxophone. Sometimes they'd use a drum machine or play along to backing tracks pre-recorded onto a cassette."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Eccentric and Quirky Style
podcast.body: They Might Be Giants are characterized as charmingly eccentric and quirky, known for the unusual references embedded in their lyrics, which appealed to alt-rock fans. "I think the word I'd use for these guys is charmingly eccentric and quirky. Fans loved the weird references in their lyrics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Geek Rock Archetype
podcast.body: They Might Be Giants were presented as an example of Geek Rock, notable for incorporating an accordion into their music while singing about subjects like astronomy and physics, embodying the genre's quirky, intellectual, and humorous approach. "They might be giants, who like to sing about astronomy and physics while busting out an accordion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Liam Lynch directed music videos for They Might Be Giants. "He went on to direct music videos for... They might be giants."
